About PhaseCraft

PhaseCraft turns the paper based ICASS Practical Assessment Task 2 (Construct a three-phase transformer in Star and Delta configurations) into a working digital verification bench for lecturers. Instead of working through a printed checklist by hand, a lecturer enters the student's multimeter readings into the app, which applies the same pass or fail logic a lecturer would apply manually, instantly and consistently.

Every screen, table and formula in PhaseCraft is drawn directly from the official assessment paperwork for this task:

Student Guide

The reviewed practical assessment instructions issued to learners for this task, including the student's checklist and mark allocations.

Lecturer Guide

The matching assessment guide issued to lecturers, including the model checklist and its sample measurement values, used here to calibrate the app's pass or fail logic so it agrees with how the task is actually marked.

Designed and built by MJ Maake.

1.2 and 1.3 Tolerance Check (2 marks)

To confirm the three transformers are functional and closely matched enough to form a three phase bank, the spread of each winding's resistance across the three units must stay within a 5 % tolerance of the average. The tolerance for a set of readings is:

$$ \text{Tolerance} = \max_i \left| \frac{R_i - \overline{R}}{\overline{R}} \right| \times 100\% $$
  • $R_i$: the winding resistance reading ($\Omega$) for transformer $i$ (where $i = 1, 2, 3$), within the same group (primary windings, or secondary windings).
  • $\overline{R}$: the average of the three readings in that group: $\overline{R} = \dfrac{R_1 + R_2 + R_3}{3}$. The bar over $R$ is standard notation for "the average of R".
  • $\max_i$: take the largest value across the three transformers (the subscript $i$ just labels which transformer, $i = 1, 2, 3$), i.e. the reading that deviates furthest from the average.
  • Tolerance: the resulting worst-case percentage deviation from the average; the checklist requires this to be $\le 5\%$ for the transformers to be considered suitably matched.

Balance Check (informational)

In a delta-connected secondary, each line voltage is taken directly across a single winding, so line voltage equals phase (winding) voltage:

$$ V_{line} = V_{phase} $$
  • $V_{line}$: the voltage measured between two secondary output lines (e.g. $L_1$-$L_2$), what your multimeter reads at the transformer's output terminals.
  • $V_{phase}$: the voltage across a single secondary winding. In a delta, each winding's two ends are directly the two line terminals, so line and phase voltage are the same value.

For a healthy, well-matched three-phase transformer bank on a balanced supply, the three measured line voltages should be close to each other. This tool checks how far the three readings spread from their average, using the same deviation method as the winding resistance check in Subtask 1:

$$ \text{Imbalance} = \max_i \left| \frac{V_i - \overline{V}} {\overline{V}} \right| \times 100\% $$
  • $V_i$: each of the three secondary line voltage readings ($L_1$-$L_2$, $L_1$-$L_3$, $L_2$-$L_3$), where $i$ ranges over these three pairs.
  • $\overline{V}$: the average of the three readings: $\overline{V} = \dfrac{V_{L_1L_2} + V_{L_1L_3} + V_{L_2L_3}}{3}$.
  • Imbalance: the largest percentage gap between any one reading and that average; kept under 5% as a rule of thumb for a healthy, balanced connection.

Star Relationship Check

In a star-connected secondary, the line voltage is the vector difference between two phase voltages 120° apart, which for a balanced three-phase system reduces to:

$$ V_{line} = \sqrt{3} \times V_{phase} $$
  • $V_{line}$: the voltage measured between two secondary output lines (e.g. $L_1$-$L_2$).
  • $V_{phase}$: the voltage measured between one secondary output line and the star (neutral) point.
  • $\sqrt{3}$: approximately 1.732, this factor comes from the 120° phase difference between windings in a balanced star connection, the line voltage is the vector (not arithmetic) difference of two phase voltages.

This tool averages your three line readings and your three phase readings, then checks whether they satisfy that root three relationship, alongside a balance check within each group (same method as Subtasks 1 and 2):

$$ \text{Imbalance}_{group} = \max_i \left| \frac{V_i - \overline{V}}{\overline{V}} \right| \times 100\% \qquad\qquad \text{Ratio error} = \left| \frac{\overline{V}_{line} - \sqrt{3}\, \overline{V}_{phase}}{\sqrt{3}\, \overline{V}_{phase}} \right| \times 100\% $$
  • $V_i$: each individual reading within a group, the three line readings ($L_1$-$L_2$, $L_1$-$L_3$, $L_2$-$L_3$) for the line group, or the three phase readings ($L_1$-$N$, $L_2$-$N$, $L_3$-$N$) for the phase group.
  • $\overline{V}$: the average of the three readings within that group.
  • $\text{Imbalance}_{group}$: the largest percentage deviation of any single reading from its group's average, checked separately for the line group and the phase group.
  • $\overline{V}_{line}$ and $\overline{V}_{phase}$: the averages of the line group and the phase group respectively.
  • Ratio error: how far the measured average line voltage sits from the theoretical $\sqrt{3} \times \overline{V}_{phase}$ prediction; a large error usually means a reading was taken between the wrong terminals.
